name: o42601

name.description: A unique identifier (within the form) for the field. This value is not shown to the user and should NOT change once set.

maps_to.description: The name of the schema field the answer will map to. By default this will go to the "cf" field which is a "dynamic-field" list containing all answers filled out on the form (ref "gdbots:forms:mixin:send-submission").

label.description: The main text for the question/field.

description.description: A short description to better explain this field.

link_text.description: The text that will replace the token "{link}" within the label or description.

link_url.description: The URL to use for the replaced token "{link}" within the label or description.

is_consent.description: If this field relates to acquiring a user's consent, e.g. subscribing to a newsletter, then this field can be used to ensure that consent is tracked.

erroneous_json.name: consent_newsletter
erroneous_json.label: Would you like to receive our newsletter?
erroneous_json.description: Check the box to receive monthly updates and promotions.

valid_json.name: consent_newsletter
valid_json.label: Would you like to receive our newsletter?
valid_json.description: Check the box to receive monthly updates and promotions.

description:
The form includes a required question identified internally as pbj:gdbots:forms:field:yes-no-field:1-0-1, with the field name **consent_newsletter**. It is mapped to the **cf** data bucket, and because the placeholder is left blank, no hint text will appear inside the control. The label presented to users reads: “Would you like to receive our newsletter?” and a brief description follows – “Check the box to receive monthly updates and promotions.” Since this is a consent‑related item ( is_consent = true ), the personal data impact has been assessed as **low**.

The response options are customized: selecting **Yes, sign me up** records consent, while **No, thanks** declines it. A link to the company’s Privacy Policy is embedded in the field text; the link text is “Privacy Policy” and it points to https://example.com/privacy. Because the field is mandatory, users must choose either the yes‑label or the no‑label before submitting the form.
